purpose: Reference high-level songwriting patterns across eras, genres, and artist technique profiles without storing or reproducing copyrighted lyrics or melodies.
guardrails: Use artist entries only as analysis labels for high-level techniques, never as instructions to imitate a living or deceased artist.
Never reproduce recognizable lyrics, melodies, signature flows, or passages from reference songs.
Measured findings and heuristic observations are labeled separately.
Hit-potential scores are songwriting diagnostics, not predictions or guarantees.

measured_priors.finding: Billboard's Top Hot 100 Songs of the 21st Century retrospective is based on weekly Hot 100 performance from the start of 2000 through the end of 2024.
measured_priors.use: Use chart performance only as a selection signal for which successful songs/eras deserve study; do not infer causation from rank alone.
measured_priors.source: Billboard / Billboard Canada, Top Hot 100 Songs of the 21st Century

measured_priors.sample: 2,487 hit songs across pop, rock, R&B/hip-hop, and country from 2011-2019
measured_priors.finding: Average first-chorus start decreased by 5.41 seconds for songs released during/after 2015; after controlling for total runtime, the average difference was 2.303 seconds earlier.
measured_priors.use: Do not assume modern hits require an immediate chorus. Favor a strong early identity, but let the beat determine whether the hook should arrive early.
measured_priors.source: UC Riverside research on streaming-era popular-song composition

measured_priors.finding: Mean duration in 2018-2023 was about 221.5 seconds versus 249.3 seconds in 2000-2009, a reduction of about 28 seconds; the tempo difference was only about 1 BPM and practically negligible.
measured_priors.use: Modern songs can be more economical, but do not shorten sections just to chase streaming. Tempo should be chosen from the beat, not era stereotypes.
measured_priors.source: Did Streaming Break How Songs Are Built? public research dataset

traits: longer average song forms than current streaming-era norms
more tolerance for intros and instrumental setup
bridges and third-act variation common across pop/rock/R&B
era_profiles.use_when: The beat develops gradually or benefits from fuller narrative progression.

traits: hook repetition balanced with full verses
rap frequently uses distinct verse flows around a stable chorus
era_profiles.use_when: The instrumental has obvious rises and drops that support section contrast.

traits: trap-influenced pocket becomes broadly dominant in rap
short title phrases and repeated motifs become especially important
looser rhyme is acceptable when vocal melody carries the section
era_profiles.use_when: The beat supports melody, half-time trap pockets, or emotionally direct repetition.

traits: strong identity early in the track
hooks may be very short and recur often
vocal texture, cadence and production can carry repetition that would look simple on paper
era_profiles.use_when: The beat is concise, loop-driven, or relies heavily on texture and replayability.

avoid: verse-level complexity leaking into the chorus

priorities: contrast between verse density and hook economy
avoid: same cadence for an entire verse
switches that ignore the drum pocket
melodies too complex for the vocalist

priorities: melody that sounds conversational rather than theatrical

avoid: too many syllables over open drums
hook language that is harder than the verse

priorities: harmonic space for doubles and harmonies
avoid: wordy phrases that fight sustained melody
choruses that read like another verse
trying to sound poetic on every line

technique_archetypes.name: melodic-conversational
traits: emotional words get the longest notes

technique_archetypes.name: cadence-switch-heavy
traits: repeated rhythm cells before each change

technique_archetypes.name: hook-first
traits: chorus language is simpler than verse language

technique_archetypes.name: hybrid-balanced
traits: hook stays simple even if verses are technical
best_for: songs that need both replayability and lyrical depth

artist_technique_profiles.translate_to_original_work: Borrow the principle of dense rhyme with semantic purpose only when the beat supports it; never imitate recognizable flows or phrasing.

strengths: smooth movement between rap and melody
artist_technique_profiles.translate_to_original_work: Favor natural speech-shaped melody and emotionally direct lines; keep concepts and phrases fully original.
Use restraint and direct emotion when the instrumental is atmospheric; do not imitate lyric topics, melodies, or signature wording.
Test compact, repeatable hook cells and unusual but natural melodic shapes without copying flows.
Use controlled rhythmic surprise where drums invite it; keep transitions musically motivated.

strengths: contrast between raw verses and sung phrases
artist_technique_profiles.translate_to_original_work: Use emotionally strong sustained words selectively and only within the vocalist's comfortable range.
Let rests and tone do work instead of adding filler; keep wording original and beat-specific.
Prioritize lines that sound natural aloud and clean transitions between rhythmic and melodic sections.
Keep technical writing understandable and make each verse progress the idea.
Use perspective and cadence changes only when they clarify the concept; never imitate recognizable voices or flows.
Prioritize a clear melodic identity and section contrast without copying melody or lyrical themes.
Blend genre techniques only when the beat supports them and keep the hook simpler than the verse.

selection_logic.step_1: Identify beat structure, energy changes, drum density, available vocal space, and likely emotional lane.
selection_logic.step_2: Choose one primary genre profile and optionally one secondary genre profile.
selection_logic.step_3: Compare at least three technique archetype blends and select the best-fitting blend.
selection_logic.step_4: Use artist technique profiles only as a checklist of high-level craft options, never as imitation targets.
selection_logic.step_5: Draft hook first, then test natural speech, memorability, melodic space, and vocal ease before writing full verses.
selection_logic.step_6: Run overfill and section-progression checks; remove words if space improves the song.
selection_logic.step_7: Score hook recall, natural phrasing, pocket, contrast, emotional clarity, originality, and replayability; revise any score below 8/10.
